annotation.title_clean: Engineering-Based Design Methodology for Embedding Ethics in Autonomous Robots
annotation.title_en: Engineering-Based Design Methodology for Embedding Ethics in Autonomous Robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Robertson, L.J.; Abbas, R.; Alici, G.; Munoz, A.; Michael, K.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article proposing an ethics-based co-design methodology for autonomous biomedical robots, illustrated by a robotic endoscopic capsule for diagnosis and drug delivery. It argues for moving beyond standard risk assessment toward measuring end-user exposure and vulnerability, involving diverse stakeholders during preclinical design.
key_provisions_or_claims: Ethics should be embedded in engineering design via stakeholder co-design, not only post hoc risk assessment.
Proposes 'exposure' as a metric of end-user vulnerability to guide design feedback.
Distinguishes present and future modes of operation to anticipate increasing autonomy.
Diverse stakeholders beyond traditional designers should be involved in preclinical biomedical design.
Design should identify positive consequences for wellbeing, not only avoid harm.
